Messages.Author: Jaysen Knight
Messages.Body:
My vamp intercepts pred's vamp, strikes aggro, sends opponent to torpor,
plays Amaranth. Opponent calls blood hunt, I play Delaying Tactics....
what happens next after blood hunt vote is cancelled?

Is the blood hunt vote gone forever now, or is it called the next turn?

(I think it is gone forever, just making sure).

Messages.Author: Jasper Phillips
Messages.Body:

Actually, I don't believe you can use Action Modifiers or Reactions
during a blood hunt, as it's called by the Methuselah, and is
explicitly not an action.

Messages.Body:
In article <3654C1AA...@arcticdata.nt.ca>, Jaysen Knight

<jay...@arcticdata.nt.ca> writes

>My vamp intercepts pred's vamp, strikes aggro, sends opponent to torpor,
>plays Amaranth. Opponent calls blood hunt, I play Delaying Tactics....
>what happens next after blood hunt vote is cancelled?
>
>Is the blood hunt vote gone forever now, or is it called the next turn?

A blood hunt is not a political action. You cannot react to it with
Delaying Tactics nor, indeed, any other reaction.

So your question is moot.

Messages.Author: Kevin Kelly
Messages.Body:
The blood hunt vote is the one thing that I have *never* been clear on.
The vote itself I get (I understand the not an action thing) but how
*exactly* is the vote called. I bet since I started playing I have
played it 8 different ways. First we played that a person (ie. meth)
just says "I call a blood hunt", then we take a vote among ourselves.
Then we played the same way to call it but used the vampire titles to
vote. At some point we said someone had to tap to call it (although
anyone could do it). This meant that if you didn't have anyone untapped
you couldn't call the BH vote.

What is the "real" way it is supposed to be done. Could someone tell me
- and please be VERY specific. I have been playing this game a long
time, I understand the rules very well BUT, I just don't get the blood
hunt.

Please help,
Kevin

PS. out current interpretation is that someone has to tap a vampire to
call the vote.

Messages.Author: Richard D. Zopf
Messages.Body:
Kevin Kelly <kke...@activecom.net> wrote:

>The blood hunt vote is the one thing that I have *never* been clear on.
>The vote itself I get (I understand the not an action thing) but how
>*exactly* is the vote called. I bet since I started playing I have
>played it 8 different ways. First we played that a person (ie. meth)
>just says "I call a blood hunt", then we take a vote among ourselves.
>Then we played the same way to call it but used the vampire titles to
>vote. At some point we said someone had to tap to call it (although
>anyone could do it). This meant that if you didn't have anyone untapped
>you couldn't call the BH vote.

>What is the "real" way it is supposed to be done. Could someone tell me
>- and please be VERY specific. I have been playing this game a long
>time, I understand the rules very well BUT, I just don't get the blood
>hunt.

> Please help,
> Kevin

>PS. out current interpretation is that someone has to tap a vampire to
>call the vote.

Step 1: Diablerie. A Vampire Diablerizes another. The diabolist gets
its victims' blood and equipment (If diabolist is younger than
victim, it gets a skill card from your hand, library, or ash heap.)

Step 2: Call Blood Hunt. Any Methuselah (Player) may "call a blood
hunt vote". This is _not_ an action, so it does not require the use
of a minion. Also, because it is not an action, action modifiers and
reaction cards may not be played in the impending referendum.

Step 3: Referendum. This vote tallying step occurs as usual. No one
needs to announce votes in any order, and votes are submitted or not
until all players are satisfied (or at least out of votes).
Applicable vote sources for a blood hunt vote include; all vampires
who have votes, any permanent card in play that provides votes
(Ventrue HQ, Alamut, etc.), the Edge, and each player may play _one_
political action card from their hand for its vote (under 7/7 vote
push rules).
Note: Sect affiliation (Camarilla/Sabbat/Independent) doesn't matter
for the purposes of providing votes to the referendum (eg. The Prisci
sub-vote happens, as normal, and the votes apply to blood hunts on
Camarilla and Independent vampires. The reverse applies for
Camarilla votes on Sabbat and Independent diabolists).

Step 4: Results. Tied votes fail, as usual. If there are more votes
in favor of burning than against, the diabolist is burned, and all
cards on it are returned to their respective owners' graveyards. If
the vote fails, the remainder of the turn progresses as normal.

Regards,
R. David Zopf

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <734o3h$2mb$1...@camel29.mindspring.com>, Richard D. Zopf
<guenh...@mindspring.com> writes

> any permanent card in play that provides votes
>(Ventrue HQ, Alamut, etc.)

Ventrue HQ = yes. It just says to tap to get votes.

Alamut = no. It has its clause to get votes DURING A POLITICAL ACTION.

The Bloodhunt Referendum does not come from a political action, so a lot
of permanents which give votes during a political action do not apply.

Messages.Author: Hardy Range
Messages.Body:
Hmmm...

I think here we have another case where the new rules have caused a problem
with some of the cards. Of course, if we follow the text on the card, James
is perfectly right, but the term "political action" on almost all of these
cards was used _before_ we had the better-defined difference between a
"political action" and the resulting "referendum" (and the Bloodhunt vote
qualifies for the latter, if I am not mistaken). Since the introduction of
this new term has already made errata and explanations necessary for other
cards (Antonio Delgado comes to my mind right now), perhaps cards like
Alamut should be reworded, too, to give them back their original
intention...

Hardy Range

In article <fTR52.737$7u3....@news1.cityweb.de>, Hardy Range
<Hardy...@cityweb.de> writes

>Since the introduction of
>this new term has already made errata and explanations necessary for other
>cards (Antonio Delgado comes to my mind right now), perhaps cards like
>Alamut should be reworded, too, to give them back their original
>intention...

The vote called in the Bloodhutn is now referred to as a referendum.

It was never referred to as a political action, made clear by the
inability to play actions and reactions to it. The new piece of
terminology has changed nothing, other than making it easier to
communicate ideas about what's going on. All cards were created in an
environment where the Bloodhunt was not a political action.

Also, minimising errata where unnecessary is a concern. I do not
believe changing these cards to be necessary.

Also, if you wish to argue intent, feel free, but the rules on Bloodhunt
votes now and then (about them not being a political action) have not
changed. I do not believe that this was the original intent of the
card.

> Alamut should be reworded, too, to give them back their original
> intention...
>

Umm... I don't know what rules change you're talking about. A bloodhunt
has never, ever been a political action, and thus action modifiers,
reactions, and effects which say "during a political action" have never
been allowed during a bloodhunt. This has been in effect since the
first publication of Jyhad and is stated outright in the Jyhad
rulebook. Thus, effects which are only usable "during a political
action" could never be used in a bloodhunt, and were almost certainly
never intended to be.

-Chris

Messages.Author: Hardy Range
Messages.Body:

"Umm... I don't know what rules change you're talking about. A bloodhunt

been allowed during a bloodhunt. This has been in effect since the
first publication of Jyhad and is stated outright in the Jyhad
rulebook. Thus, effects which are only usable "during a political
action" could never be used in a bloodhunt, and were almost certainly
never intended to be."

This reply also addresses the post from James, who had the same opinion, but
in different words...

I absolutely agree with what you say about the Bloodhunt never being a
political vote - but I did not want to argue that. In my opinion, the
problem is hidden in the last sentence of your post: Yes, those cards were
perhaps not intended to be used in a Bloodhunt, but I think this is not by
intention, but because they just overlooked that possibility. And I did not
want to limit my ideas to the Bloodhunt - I think the problem is with the
other cards.

The "rules change" (or call it clarification) I refer to is the better
definition of the political action itself and the following referendum,
making them two separate things (that, of course, are linked...). The ruling
which set my thoughts in motion was the following one:

"An action is successful if it is unblocked and uncancelled, even if it has
no other effect. An unblocked bleed of zero or less is an unsuccessful
bleed, but is a successful action. An unblocked political action is
successful even if the referendum fails. The cost, if any, of an action is
paid if the action is successful, regardless of these other factors. [RTR
980623] "

I still think that all of those cards that say "gain votes during a poltical
action" have been worded without this difference in mind (hence the changes
for some cards I mentioned in my original post). If you interpret the rules
in an extreme way, you just cannot use any vote-giving effect during a
political action (the action to call a referendum)- votes are only allowed
in the actual referendum, and that was why I had the feeling that those
handful of cards are somewhat unclear (and _perhaps_ could be reworded.
James, I totally agree with you that errata should only be issued when
necessary - it is difficult enough for me to catch up with the newest
rulings as it is, especially since I translate them to German for my friends
and co-players, only to find that the day after I handed the new version
out, the three web-pages have been revamped...sigh...).

Hardy Range

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
> The "rules change" (or call it clarification) I refer to is the better
> definition of the political action itself and the following referendum,
> making them two separate things (that, of course, are linked...). The ruling
> which set my thoughts in motion was the following one:
>
> "An action is successful if it is unblocked and uncancelled, even if it has
> no other effect. An unblocked bleed of zero or less is an unsuccessful
> bleed, but is a successful action. An unblocked political action is
> successful even if the referendum fails. The cost, if any, of an action is
> paid if the action is successful, regardless of these other factors. [RTR
> 980623] "
>

Well, first off, clarifications are never rules changes, but simply an
answer
to someone's confusion. Usually the clarification is unnecessary, as
the correct answer is obvious.

In this case, the clarification was issued to overturn an early ruling
that linked too strongly the referendum to the political action and the
bleed amount to the acttion.

The earlier clarification (or ruling, or whatever) said that a bleed of
0 or less was unsuccessful, and there was never any statement as to
whether a vote had to pass to be a successful action.

The only difference this makes is that when a political action is
called, an action is considered to have been successful (where
successful is synonomous with "unblocked"). This is necessary with
cards like Freak Drive (the inferior requires a successful action, the
superior a block... if an unblocked political action or bleed could be
unsuccessful, there's kind of a contradiction).

This didn't change the relationship between a political action and the
referendum. Or between Bloodhunts and political actions. A political
action is, and always has been a vote called as an action. A Bloodhunt
has never been called as an action. The clarification that you quote
has not changed this, and neither has any other clarification.

-Chris
